newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bank staff march, inspired by Cr Foncier.
newsitem.headline: French bank staff march, inspired by Cr Foncier.

text.p: Around 1,000 French bank employees and trade union leaders marched through central Paris on Tuesday in a show of solidarity with staff occupying the troubled bank Credit Foncier and to demand a halt to job losses.

The protest rally organised by trade unions at 14 state and semi-state banks started at the headquarters of Credit Foncier, which was being occupied for a 12th day by employees fighting to save the home loans bank from government plans to break it up.
The protestors moved on to the Paris stock exchange, where heavily armed riot police were waiting, but dispersed without incident.

Unions organising the wider bank sector protest told a news conference in front of Credit Foncier that they would organise a "major national initiative" in the coming weeks against job cuts due to restructuring in the sector.
"Saving jobs is urgent, to preserve a public service for the nation and public instruments used to finance and support the economy," said Jean-Christophe Chaumeron of the Communist-led CGT union.

Richard Maupied, a Socialist CFDT union delegate at Credit Foncier, said that 80,000 jobs were at risk in the sector and that France should fight for a specifically French society in which "(financial) markets are not everything".

At Credit Foncier 3,300 employees are campaigning to halt plans unveiled by Finance Minister Jean Arthuis in July to have their bank partially taken over by a rival, cooperatively run group, Credit Immobilier, and the rest shut over time.

Their sit-in began on January 17, inspiring wider protest, including Tuesday's demonstration and a board meeting invasion by 100 staff on Monday at state insurer Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance (CNP) who fear job losses as the government prepares CNP for privatisation.
